response.sql: SELECT store_id, AVG(total_amount) AS avg_total_amount_per_rental, AVG(payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental FROM (SELECT i.store_id AS store_id, p.rental_id AS rental_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(*) AS payment_count FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id WHERE p.amount > 4.99 GROUP BY i.store_id, p.rental_id) t GROUP BY store_id

assumptions.assumption: The 'more than 4.99' filter is applied to each individual payment amount (strictly greater than 4.99) before totaling and counting per rental, not to the per-rental totals.
Inner joins from payment to rental to inventory implement 'leave out payments without such a match'; payments with NULL rental_id are dropped.
